correctness.rationale: Row/column unitary factors and conjugation reduce the symbol to the stated angle with no change of ratio. With F the squared Frobenius norm and u,v the absolute normalized input/output determinants, the identities in (1) follow from the sum and product of the squared singular values. Solving for the two normalized products gives the sum-of-distances constraint with foci uc±iuh (c=cos(δ/2), h=sin(δ/2)); AM–GM ensures every matrix satisfies the constraint. The boundary modulus squared is a concave quadratic in cos φ. Its vertex is feasible exactly for u≥c (apart from the harmless degenerate endpoints), giving v_max=1 there and v_max=uc+h√(1−u²) below. Substitution into the 2s₂ branch yields a nondecreasing bound below c (the derivative numerator is c(1+u)/√(1−u²)+h−1≥0) and the decreasing square bound 2/(1+u) above. The s₁ branch is at most one by Frobenius invariance. The witness has F=4, u=c and v=1, so it gives exactly sec(δ/4), including δ=π where c=0. The δ=0 map preserves singular values and rank one gives equality. Cross-ratio one is exactly row-times-column phase factorization; Taylor expansion gives 1+δ²/32+O(δ⁴).
